newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. source punctures Libya balloon claim.
newsitem.headline: U.N. source punctures Libya balloon claim.

text.p: A U.N. sanctions committee source on Tuesday rejected a claim by Libya that it was no longer subject to U.N. air sanctions after it gave permission for a balloon to overfly its territory last week.
"It's a lot of hot air," the source said when asked about the Libyan assertion, made in a letter to the Security Council.

Though the letter had not yet been translated from the Arabic and circulated to council members, press reports said Libya wrote that it first denied permission for American balloonist Steve Fossett to overfly Libyan territory on Friday because of sanctions imposed in connection with the 1988 bombing of an airliner over Lockerbie, Scotland.
But Libya then altered its position and allowed him to pass over its territory.
According to his control centre in Chicago, he was over Libya for an hour and 45 minutes though the detour and loss of fuel forced him to cut short his attempted around-the-world flight in India.
Libya was reported to have said that, after giving Fossett overflight permission, it would now allow any aircraft to fly in and out of the country.

The U.N. source said the 1992 Security Council resolution imposing air sanctions on Libya for failing to extradite two men wanted in the Lockerbie bombing said nothing about a ban on overflying Libyan territory.

The resolution, number 748, requires all countries to deny permission to any aircraft to take off from, land in or overfly their territory if it is destined to land in, or has taken off from, Libyan territory.
